(a) Provision of Off-base Transition Training.—During the two-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Labor shall provide the Transition Assistance Program under section 1144 of title 10, United States Code, to eligible individuals at locations other than military installations to assess the feasibility and advisability of providing such program to eligible individuals at locations other than military installations. 
    (b) Eligible Individuals.—For purposes of this section, an eligible individual is a veteran or the spouse of a veteran. 
    (c) Locations.—
        (1) Number of states.—The Secretary shall carry out the training under subsection (a) in not less than three and not more than five States selected by the Secretary for purposes of this section. 
        (2) Selection of states with high unemployment.—Of the States selected by the Secretary under paragraph (1), at least two shall be States with high rates of unemployment among veterans. 
        (3) Number of locations in each state.—The Secretary shall provide training under subsection (a) to eligible individuals at a sufficient number of locations within each State selected under this subsection to meet the needs of eligible individuals in such State. 
        (4) Selection of locations.—The Secretary shall select locations for the provision of training under subsection (a) to facilitate access by participants and may not select any location on a military installation other than a National Guard or reserve facility that is not located on an active duty military installation.  
    (d) Inclusion of Information About Veterans Benefits.—The Secretary shall ensure that the training provided under subsection (a) generally follows the content of the Transition Assistance Program under section 1144 of title 10, United States Code. 
    (e) Annual Report.—Not later than March 1 of any year during which the Secretary provides training under subsection (a), the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the provision of such training. 
    (f) Comptroller General Report.—Not later than 180 days after the termination of the one-year period described in subsection (a), the Comptroller General of the United States shall submit to Congress a report on the training provided under such subsection. The report shall include the evaluation of the Comptroller General regarding the feasibility and advisability of carrying out off-base transition training at locations nationwide.

fable.w: The tempting reading treats the reports, the selection of States, and the reference to "participants" as participation. The reports go only to Congress, which is inside the federal government, and the Secretary of Labor selects States and locations unilaterally, with no required consultation with States or other outside parties. Veterans and spouses are recipients of a training program, not consulted parties in a federal decision, and there is no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the provision of such training.

qwen_block.w: This section mandates the Secretary of Labor to provide training services to veterans and their spouses. It does not require the government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from these individuals or any other outside parties before making a decision. The 'eligible individuals' are recipients of a service, not participants in a decision-making process. The reports mentioned are submitted to Congress, which is inside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary of Labor shall provide the Transition Assistance Program... to eligible individuals at locations other than military installations

opus.w: The Secretary of Labor alone chooses the States and training locations, and nothing requires consulting the States, the public or outside experts first. The "participants" are veterans and spouses who receive training, not people with input into a federal decision. The annual report and the Comptroller General's report both go to Congress, so that interaction stays inside the federal government and is not participation.
opus.s: The Secretary shall select locations for the provision of training under subsection (a) to facilitate access by participants
opus.b: The tempting reading is to call this participation because the text mentions "participants," selects States, and requires reports. That reading fails. The "participants" are veterans and spouses receiving training, which is a service, not a say in a federal decision. The Secretary picks the States and locations alone, without consulting them. The reports go to Congress, which is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of Labor to provide training to veterans and requires reports to Congress. The selection of states and locations is made solely by the Secretary. There is no requirement to consult with state governments, local entities, or the public before making these decisions. The veterans receiving training are beneficiaries, not participants in the decision-making process as defined.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall carry out the training under subsection (a) in not less than three and not more than five States selected by the Secretary for purposes of this section.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "participants" in the training program (veterans and spouses) are involved in a federal decision. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or participation in programs/services from counting as "participation" in the sense of consulting with outsiders before a decision. The veterans are recipients of a service, not advisors or stakeholders consulted on policy. The reports are sent to Congress (inside government). There is no consultation with states, tribes, or the public regarding the *decision* to provide the training or how it is structured, other than the Secretary's internal selection of locations.
